name: NJ-05
label: Safe D

key_factors: Gottheimer's massive financial advantage ($12.8M cash vs ~$8K)
Markets price Gottheimer at 93-95% to win
Incumbency in a district that leans Democratic by 2 points
No public polling of the general election
model.rationale: Gottheimer holds a huge cash and incumbency edge in a district that leans Democratic, and both Kalshi and Polymarket price his reelection at 93-95 percent. With no polling and a little-known, minimally funded challenger, the fundamentals point to a comfortable but not landslide margin.
model.watch: A late surge of outside spending against Gottheimer or a strong national Republican environment could narrow the margin.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Josh Gottheimer seeks another term in a northern New Jersey district that voted slightly Democratic at the presidential level. He has raised about $4.8 million and holds nearly $12.8 million on hand, while Republican Sean Kirrane has raised under $60,000 with almost nothing banked. No outside groups have meaningfully engaged, and no public polls cover the race.

Prediction markets give Gottheimer a 93 to 95 percent chance of winning, and the seat's fundamentals favor the incumbent. The forecast calls this Safe D with an expected margin in the high teens, though the absence of polling keeps uncertainty somewhat elevated.
